hook.text: Putting all your money in one stock is like putting all your eggs in one basket—and hoping nobody bumps the table.

buildup.text: Diversification spreads capital across multiple assets so that no single failure can devastate the portfolio.

discovery.text: Owning 20 uncorrelated stocks reduces portfolio volatility dramatically compared to owning just one or two.

twist.text: Over-diversification dilutes returns. Owning 100 stocks mimics the index—you're paying fees for market-average results.

climax.text: The sweet spot is 15–30 positions across different sectors. Enough protection without giving up all upside.

punchline.text: Diversify enough to survive, not so much you can't win.

quiz.question: Why is over-diversification a problem?
options: It dilutes returns and mimics the market index
